script.text: France's borrowing costs are near their highest since 2002. Why do riots move markets?

On Monday, French bond yields rose by more than a tenth of a percentage point, CNBC reports. The ten-year yield reached about 4.9 percent. Reuters says its peak in early October, 4.99 percent, was the highest since 2002. The CAC 40 closed down 1.1 percent.

Reuters ties the move to weekend riots, with thousands arrested. Investors doubt that Prime Minister Lecornu's minority government can pass the 2027 budget and cut the deficit, CNBC says. A bond yield is simply what a state pays to borrow.

The gap over German yields hit 146 basis points, Reuters says. BNP Paribas and Societe Generale each fell about 3 percent in Monday trading. The euro slipped too. Moody's is due to review France's credit rating on Friday.
Will France's borrowing costs top five percent again? Yes or no?
